skill.name: when-bridging-web-cli-use-web-cli-teleport
skill.description: Plan a web-to-CLI bridge that connects web interfaces with CLI workflows through REST APIs and WebSockets.
skill.summary: Guides teams through building a bidirectional bridge between browser interfaces and command-line automation.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The skill documents a useful web-to-CLI bridge pattern, but the sample implementation includes browser-accessible command execution through child_process.exec. Several static findings are Markdown formatting false positives, yet the confirmed execution endpoint, permissive Socket.io bridge, and output broadcast create critical security concerns if copied as written.

remediation.suggestion: Replace free-form command strings with an allowlist of fixed commands. Use spawn with argument arrays, disable shell execution, validate every argument, and add execution timeouts.

remediation.issue: Unauthenticated bridge service and permissive CORS
remediation.suggestion: Require authentication, restrict allowed origins, bind development services to trusted interfaces, and add rate limits before exposing any bridge endpoint.

remediation.issue: Command output is broadcast to all clients
remediation.suggestion: Send command output only to the authenticated requester or a scoped Socket.io room. Redact secrets and avoid broadcasting stdout globally.

remediation.issue: Documentation presents insecure examples as normal workflow
remediation.suggestion: Move unsafe examples into a clearly labeled prototype section and add secure default code for validation, authorization, logging, and command allowlisting.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Web Endpoint Executes Shell Commands
semantic_findings.description: The sample bridge server enables permissive CORS, accepts command and args from an HTTP request, builds a shell command string, and executes it. This design can allow browser-accessible arbitrary command execution if used without authentication, allowlisting, and strict validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The server code and quick-start examples directly show command payloads reaching the execution endpoint. The implementation has no authentication or command allowlist in the cited lines.

semantic_findings.title: Command Output Broadcast to All Socket Clients
semantic_findings.description: The server emits command stdout to all connected Socket.io clients after execution. Command output can contain secrets or filesystem details, so broadcasting it without client isolation can leak sensitive data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Socket.io server is configured with a permissive origin and the command handler emits stdout globally. The cited code does not scope output to an authenticated session or room.

content.value_statement: Teams often need a web UI to trigger and observe CLI workflows. This skill provides a bridge pattern using REST endpoints, WebSockets, and local CLI integration.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a phased architecture for web-to-CLI and CLI-to-web communication.
Provides sample React code for submitting CLI commands to an API.
Provides a Node.js Express and Socket.io bridge server example.
Shows bash examples for sending CLI analysis results to a web UI.
Defines integration test examples for REST and WebSocket flows.
limitations: The sample server executes arbitrary commands and needs hardening before use.
Examples target localhost development and do not provide production authentication.
It assumes Node.js, React, Docker, and Claude Flow are available.
It is guidance documentation, not a packaged working application.

use_cases.title: Prototype Internal CLI Dashboards
use_cases.description: Design a local dashboard that starts approved CLI tasks and streams their progress to a browser.

use_cases.title: Connect Web Tools to Local Automation
use_cases.description: Plan how a React interface can call local automation through a controlled bridge API.

use_cases.title: Plan Bidirectional Developer Tooling
use_cases.description: Map how CLI tools can send analysis results back to a live web interface.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Local Prototype Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a development-only bridge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a local web-to-CLI bridge for my project. List the web app, bridge server, CLI command flow, and basic test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Secure Command Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate hardening of the command execution model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to redesign the bridge so it only runs approved commands. Include authentication, argument validation, timeouts, and audit logging.

prompt_templates.title: Design Live Status Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design WebSocket status updates for CLI jobs. Keep each user session isolated and describe how command output reaches only the requester.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a planned web-CLI bridge for production readiness. Identify unsafe assumptions, missing controls, and safer implementation patterns.

output_examples.input: Plan a browser interface that runs approved local test commands.
output: A phased bridge architecture with a React control surface, a local API, and a restricted command runner.
A security checklist covering authentication, command allowlists, argument validation, and output scoping.
A test plan for REST requests, WebSocket updates, error handling, and timeout behavior.

output_examples.input: Review my web-to-CLI bridge design before implementation.
output: A risk summary for command execution, network exposure, and output leakage.
Recommended changes that replace free-form shell commands with fixed actions.
Deployment notes for local binding, logging, rate limits, and monitoring.

best_practices: Require authentication and allowlisted commands before exposing any execution endpoint.
Use fixed argument arrays and avoid shell command strings for command runners.
Keep bridge services bound to trusted interfaces and log every request.
anti_patterns: Do not expose a free-form command field to browsers or remote users.
Do not broadcast command output to every connected client.
Do not treat localhost examples as production security controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you plan a bridge between a web interface and command-line workflows using REST APIs and WebSockets.

faq.question: Does it include a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture steps and sample snippets that need project-specific implementation.

faq.question: Can I use the sample server in production?
faq.answer: Not as written. The command execution example needs authentication, allowlists, validation, and output isolation first.

faq.question: Which tools does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes Node.js, React, Socket.io, Docker examples, and optional Claude Flow commands.

faq.question: Why does the audit report security concerns?
faq.answer: The examples show a web endpoint that can run CLI commands. That pattern is powerful but dangerous without strict controls.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools for using the guidance.
